title: Apps are not removed from Favorites database when uninstalled which lowers the amount of Favorites that can be saved
line: Favorites in Kickoff and Kicker no longer disappear at login when some favorited apps have been uninstalled.
explanation: Kicker's favorites model loads linked favorites from the activity database with a query limited to 100 results. Entries for apps that are no longer installed are still returned by that query and only dropped afterwards as invalid, so they use up slots and push real favorites past the limit; those favorites vanish after every restart even though they are still saved. The change removes the limit from that query (Limit(0) means no LIMIT clause), so every valid favorite is loaded; stale links are still kept, as cwo asked, so favorites on unmounted or network apps are not lost.

commits.message:
applets/kicker: don't limit the favorites query to 100 entries

Favorites of apps that are no longer installed stay linked and still
counted toward the query's limit of 100 even though they are dropped
afterwards, pushing valid favorites out. Load all linked favorites.

BUG: 506578

patches.diff:
From 49c85628da07aad8bae2db4a2cd0cc20ff77681f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 02:38:19 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/kicker: don't limit the favorites query to 100
 entries

Favorites of apps that are no longer installed stay linked and still
counted toward the query's limit of 100 even though they are dropped
afterwards, pushing valid favorites out. Load all linked favorites.

BUG: 506578
---
 applets/kicker/kastatsfavoritesmodel.cpp | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/applets/kicker/kastatsfavoritesmodel.cpp b/applets/kicker/kastatsfavoritesmodel.cpp
index 224337a54c..9758139565 100644
--- a/applets/kicker/kastatsfavoritesmodel.cpp
+++ b/applets/kicker/kastatsfavoritesmodel.cpp
@@ -173,7 +173,7 @@ public:
 
     Private(KAStatsFavoritesModel *parent, const QString &clientId)
         : q(parent)
-        , m_query(LinkedResources | Agent{AGENT_APPLICATIONS, AGENT_DOCUMENTS} | Type::any() | Activity::current() | Activity::global() | Limit(100))
+        , m_query(LinkedResources | Agent{AGENT_APPLICATIONS, AGENT_DOCUMENTS} | Type::any() | Activity::current() | Activity::global() | Limit(0))
         , m_watcher(m_query)
         , m_clientId(clientId)
     {
--

media.caption: Master, 100 uninstalled favorites still linked: after restarting plasmashell, Google Chrome is missing from Favorites.
Same database with the fix: Google Chrome is shown again with all other favorites.

review.text: Removing the arbitrary Limit(100) from KAStatsFavoritesModel's linked-resources query cleanly fixes the root cause where uninstalled favorites still in ResourceLink pushed valid favorites past the 100-row cutoff on startup, while preserving stale links as requested by cwo so removable or network apps are not lost. The one-line change is safe, has no lifetime or performance concerns for user-favorited items, and the before/after verification clearly proves the fix. (Minor non-blocking nit: Limit::all() or omitting Limit is slightly more self-documenting than Limit(0), though equivalent.)

reviews.text: Removing the arbitrary Limit(100) from KAStatsFavoritesModel's linked-resources query cleanly fixes the root cause where uninstalled favorites still in ResourceLink pushed valid favorites past the 100-row cutoff on startup, while preserving stale links as requested by cwo so removable or network apps are not lost. The one-line change is safe, has no lifetime or performance concerns for user-favorited items, and the before/after verification clearly proves the fix. (Minor non-blocking nit: Limit::all() or omitting Limit is slightly more self-documenting than Limit(0), though equivalent.)

It fixes the actual cause cwo found in c15/c20: Limit(100) was applied in SQL before invalid (uninstalled) entries were dropped, so stale links pushed valid favorites out at load. ResultSet only adds a LIMIT clause when limit > 0, so Limit(0) loads every linked favorite. The query is used only through ResultSet and ResultWatcher, never ResultModel, where 0 would mean empty. Stale rows are kept on purpose, following cwo's c22 objection to auto-removal, and the harm in the current title (fewer favorites can be kept) is gone. The reporter's c24 request to raise the cap is also covered. The before/after screenshots on the same 100-stale-link database are convincing.
